summary: Modifies the previous policy for scheduling IMP and TIP down time.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 622 updates the process for notifying sites about planned IMP or TIP downtime. Organizations can name a secondary person whom the Network Control Center will call after scheduling downtime with the primary contact.

questions: how did the ncc schedule imp downtime
who can be a secondary contact
subtitle: A change to how the Network Control Center notifies sites about IMP or TIP downtime.

tldr.problem: The Network Control Center schedules some IMP or TIP downtime outside preventive-maintenance periods, and the existing contact process did not always reach all affected organizations.
tldr.mechanism: The primary site contact remains the main representative, while any host organization may nominate a secondary contact to receive a telephone call after downtime is scheduled.
tldr.outcome: The note explains how to submit a secondary contact's name and telephone number and lists current primary contacts.

today: The unit records RFC 622's status as Unknown and lists no updates or obsoleting RFCs. It documents an operational notification policy for scheduled network equipment downtime.

sections.title: Scheduling IMP and TIP Downtime
sections.content:
An IMP or TIP may need to be taken out of service outside its scheduled preventive-maintenance period, for example for retrofit work or diagnosis and repair of intermittent problems. The Network Control Center had scheduled these periods with the affected site's primary contact, who was treated as representing all connected Hosts and TIP users.

McKenzie says that the growing number of Very Distant Hosts and complaints from other host representatives prompted a review of the procedure. The primary contact arrangement remains in place.
sections.plainLanguage: The Network Control Center continues to arrange equipment downtime with a site's primary contact. The note adds a way for another organization to request a separate phone notification.

sections.title: Nominating a Secondary Contact
sections.content:
Any Host organization that wants a telephone notice when its IMP or TIP downtime is scheduled may nominate a secondary contact. The organization must provide that person's name and a telephone number where they can be reached.

Details may be sent by US mail to the Network Control Center at BBN, through the Journal system using Ident AAM, or by network mail to MCKENZIE at BBN-TENEX. NCC operators telephone the secondary contact after they schedule the downtime with the primary contact.
sections.plainLanguage: An organization can name someone else for the NCC to call about scheduled downtime. It sends the person's name and phone number by mail, the Journal system or network mail.

sections.title: Primary Site Contacts
sections.content:
The RFC lists the current primary site contacts and, where supplied, backup primary contacts for network locations. The list includes the named representatives for sites such as UCLA, SRI, UCSB, BBN, MIT-MAC, Harvard, Stanford, Hawaii and London.

The memo asks sites to report if their primary contact should be changed. The contact list supports the scheduling process described in the note.
sections.plainLanguage: The note publishes the people currently listed as each site's primary contact. Sites are asked to report changes to those contact details.
